_meta.what_this_is: Paired A/B scores over the same 30 held-out cases from evals-basic-01. System A is the baseline Query prompt; System B adds one grounding instruction ('cite a page for every claim or refuse'). Each case is graded by the six-check rubric from evals-basic-01; the stored number is checks_passed out of 6. The two systems ran on the SAME cases, so the scores are paired: row F03 is system A's grade and system B's grade on the identical question.
_meta.how_scores_were_produced: Fixture. These are stored grades, not live model calls, so every run of compare.py prints the same point estimates. The bootstrap and permutation numbers are seeded (seed=0), so they are identical run to run too. Substituting your own runs.json is the whole exercise; see the Build section of the module.
_meta.why_paired: Pairing is the point of the module. Because both systems answered the same 30 questions, the difference can be measured case by case, and whatever made a case hard for A tends to make it hard for B too. That shared difficulty cancels in the per-case subtraction but not in the two separate means.
_meta.regressions_kept: Two cases where B scored BELOW A are left in on purpose (F06, S02). A real prompt change helps most cases and hurts a few; hiding the losses would fake the significance test.
